dossier.deep_context:
# 2024-368: technical mechanisms, design reasoning and revision boundaries

These notes distinguish published construction from team-stated intent and original engineering inference. Selected numerical values are reported source data, not independently reproduced measurements. The recommended tests have not been performed. A binder snapshot does not certify every competition version.

## Team Kika Mana: technical sheet supports construction, not a complete design history

Version: Team Kika Mana 2024. [PDF p1](https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/f88CQDlOmk8KBTSeom6DQOruSVt.pdf#page=1)

**Published construction:** Asymmetric 3-inch Colson shooter; side-compression feed; rack hood; elevator-mounted scoring package.

**Team-stated reason or evidence boundary:** The sheet attributes spin to shot accuracy; broader selection reasoning is not documented.

**Engineering analysis — original inference:** This source is useful for geometry and component identification but should not be promoted to a full engineering binder. Different wheel count or speed across the note can create spin; compression controls the contact state and must remain consistent through the feed. A moving scorer adds position and angle errors that require joint calibration. The exact tolerance, rejected alternatives and event-by-event revision history are not established by one illustrated sheet. The agent should use it to locate a mechanism family and then seek CAD, interviews or team replies before claiming why every dimension was selected.

**Proposed validation — not a completed test:** Validate wheel arrangement and compression in CAD, then test dispersion and elevator deflection across the intended scoring range.

**Limits:** One-page technical sheet only. Complete trade studies, final reductions and season revision history remain unverified.

## Selected published parameters

| Component | Source parameter | Locator |
|---|---|---|
| Source sheet | 31.5×26-in base; L4 SDS; 3-in Colsons; 1.67× speed-up; 18.75:1 climb | [Source p1](https://www.chiefdelphi.com/uploads/short-url/f88CQDlOmk8KBTSeom6DQOruSVt.pdf#page=1) |

Ratios preserve source notation; verify driver/driven order, complete geometry and the actual version in CAD before fabrication. Figure records retain PDF page and crop bounds in `data/mechanism_images.jsonl`. Images may include rejected prototypes or whole-robot photographs; their captions preserve that distinction.

source_reviews.title: Team Kika Mana 368 2024 spec sheet
source_reviews.locator: Single page, labeled whole robot and four mechanism renderings
source_reviews.review_basis: Extracted text and visually inspected rendered page.
facts: 31.5 by 26 inch, 115 pound Falcon SDS L4 platform. 1.5 inch collector roller, double-stage feeder elevator, 10 DP shooter rack, two Falcon-driven rope climbers. The shooter pivot actuates the climber ratchet.
source_reviews.limitations: Team specification and illustrative renderings. Exact geometry, revision tags, code and live motion were not independently inspected.

source_reviews.title: Team Kika Mana 368 — 2024 Robot
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the reveal, Los Angeles recap, wheel rationale and bumper fabrication reply.
facts: Added shooter motor and wheel speed for wing-line accuracy after Los Angeles; strengthened front and replaced bumpers after stage contact. Predeployment and climb speed increase targeted a quicker Trap. The 3–1 wheel split intentionally adds spin.
source_reviews.limitations: Sub-three-second Trap was a target in the post. It is not a timed result.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Kika Mana keeps floor collection below the bumper and concentrates scoring in a taller assembly between independent climb uprights. A rack-driven variable-angle shooter delivers Speaker shots. A three-roller feeder on a double-stage extrusion elevator handles Amp and Trap and also conditions the ring before it reaches the shooter. The climb has its own motors but shares a mechanical dependency with the shooter pivot: the pivot actuates a ratchet. That interface means a complete design review must cover shot poses, chain engagement, and how the suspended frame reacts at the scoring opening.
source_review.piece_flow: The front roller combines silicone-covered contact and modified flex wheels. Passive rollers center the ring as it feeds inward. In the tower, side rollers precompress the note for the shooter, which has specified vertical and side compression. For Amp and Trap the feeder itself is the scoring assembly, using its three traction-covered rollers and changing height on the elevator. The sheet establishes those branches and contacts; it does not show the exact staging sensors, feed motor direction, or the sequence that decides when the ring has passed the branch.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The rectangular drivebase supports the low collector, central shooter and feeder structure, and two tall hook channels. The sheet shows diagonals taking the tall assembly back toward the base. That suggests stiffness is critical for both scoring alignment and climb load transfer. The bumper jog accommodates the front intake opening. The team describes stretching a single loop of fabric around the perimeter, using pleats and relief cuts where the height changes. A clearance check should include bumper deflection under contact and the envelope of the moving reaction bar.

subsystems.name: Chassis, bumpers and acquisition
subsystems.construction: 31.5 by 26 inch frame with Falcon SDS L4 and black neoprene. One 1.5-inch collector roller uses silicone tubing and modified flex wheels. Passive rollers center the note.
subsystems.operation: Floor pickup threads the note under the bumper, then passive guidance brings it into the feeder corridor.
subsystems.team_rationale: Team selected the protected layout to limit driving damage and passive centering for quick feeding. It strengthened the front after stage contact.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The bumper protects the roller from direct horizontal contact only where its deflection and the obstacle geometry leave clearance. Test a low oblique impact as well as head-on driving.
subsystems.interfaces: Floor and bumper gap determine ring entry, while collector support stiffness maintains alignment to the passive guide and feeder.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect the front-end support and bumper fit after a stage hit. Test pickup with an off-center ring before returning it to play.
subsystems.unknowns: Actual entry opening and front-end material changes between events.

subsystems.name: Feeder and Amp/Trap elevator
subsystems.construction: Three 1.25-inch rollers wrapped with self-fusing electrical tape, side precompression rollers and a double-stage extrusion elevator.
subsystems.operation: The feeder guides a note toward Speaker launch and can present and eject it for Amp or Trap.
subsystems.team_rationale: Team attributes the side rollers to precompressing the note for the shooter. The spec sheet identifies the feeder as the Amp and Trap scorer.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: The note changes support and width at the shooter mouth. Variable precompression may shift the first wheel engagement to one side, changing spin or yaw.
subsystems.interfaces: Feeder exit must overlap the shooter inlet at the transfer pose, and the elevated outlet must clear the respective scoring lip.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check tape wear and extrusion alignment, then test the handoff at both loaded and unloaded extension positions.
subsystems.unknowns: Elevator drive, extension, sensor layout and note routing timing.

subsystems.name: Pivoting Speaker shooter
subsystems.construction: 3-inch Colsons in a 3–1 lateral split, dual Falcons with 1.67× speed increase, 10 DP rack. Team lists 0.5 inch compression and 2 inches of side compression.
subsystems.operation: Automatic ranging selects a shot using the pivot and launcher. The documented range extends from bumper to wing line.
subsystems.team_rationale: The asymmetric wheel contact intentionally imparts spin for shot stability. The second motor and higher speed targeted a better wing-line shot, especially in auto.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A spin-inducing offset is only repeatable if the feeder stages the note laterally. Motor count and speed alone cannot establish dispersion.
subsystems.interfaces: Rack stiffness and support affect release elevation; pivot movement also acts on the climber ratchet.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect rack play and tooth contact after endgame loading. Compare left/right rim wear after an extended shot test.
subsystems.unknowns: Shot map, sensor feedback and rack mesh adjustment procedure.

subsystems.name: Independent climbers and reaction bar
subsystems.construction: Falcon on each side with 18.75:1 reduction, UHMWPE rope on a 1.5-inch-diameter pulley, ratchet actuated by shooter pivot and delayed reaction-bar deployment.
subsystems.operation: Team describes automatic alignment and Trap sequencing, with hook predeployment and later reaction bar timing.
subsystems.team_rationale: Delay and higher speed were pursued to shorten climb and Trap cycle time.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Hook load asymmetry can roll the suspended robot and shift the feeder away from its target despite correct extension.
subsystems.interfaces: Chain, hook, rope pulley, ratchet and reaction bar define the suspended pose while the feeder presents the note.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect rope winding and ratchet engagement individually, including off-center chain contact.
subsystems.unknowns: Ratchet phase, reaction bar timing and event-level Trap timings.

revisions: After Los Angeles, the team reported hook predeployment, 20% faster climb-related actuation, dual-motor shooter changes, front reinforcement and new autonomous modes.
transferable_principles: Size the feeder and launcher as a pair using the loaded ring shape.
Test shared pivot/ratchet functions through every relevant transition.
disconfirming_conditions: If off-axis chain engagement causes substantial roll, nominal elevator reach overstates scoring clearance.
If stage contact shifts the front structure, bumper-protected intake still needs impact reinforcement.
remaining_gaps: No primary code, full CAD, time study or measurements of scoring dispersion were reviewed.

recommended_images.subject: Labeled shooter rack, feeder tower, intake and climber renderings
Bumper jog and fabric relief cuts
